about: Every staging build, newest first. The top version always matches package.json. Each entry's checks are what to run on staging before a promote. releases.title: Shortcut stand-in: answers come back whole, ChatGPT joins, and a shorter set of writing rules
items: 🔀 Fix: the shortcut's answer now comes back on your clipboard with one Paste tap. It used to ride in the link, and the link arrived cut at about 200 characters, so every shortcut prompt was a stub that the app then padded with stock lines.

Write with (dev tools) now sits right under Build my prompt instead of in More options, and adds ChatGPT, which runs through Apple's ChatGPT extension, so with that choice your words go to OpenAI. Run stats tag it shortcut-chatgpt. Cloud Pro was tried and taken out: it answered too many requests every time.

The shortcut gets a shorter set of writing rules than Flash: six plain rules, numbers as digits, and the must-keep list last. Your core, memory, lessons, and picked My context still go along, each in a compact form. Flash is not changed.
The page snaps to the hand-off card as soon as it shows, so you aren't left watching the pot.
An answer that is very short or stops mid-sentence is held as cut off instead of being used, with Run shortcut again, another model, Use Flash instead, or Use it anyway.
The hand-off card offers the other two models (like Try ChatGPT and Try On-Device), plus Use Flash instead.

Fix: the dock now re-measures on scroll, so Rebuild shows next to Copy prompt after you change your words and scroll down, even on a slow device. Two test checks that failed on the 11/11 staging runs were steadied.

🏋️ Bench builder (dev tools, under the Flow bench): makes new grader bench cases with one copy out and one paste back. 6 notes get Read, Clean, and the fact ledger, one tap hands every write to the STP Bench Runner shortcut (2 each on ChatGPT, Cloud, and On-Device), Paste results runs Polish, the phone adds 2 seeded flaws, and Copy for answer key shows at 8 of 8. A missing or cut-off answer can be rerun on its own.

releases.title: Save as context, and a Quick version button that stays for the whole build
items: 🧱 Save as context: when your words hold background you'd otherwise retype (your job, a project, a setup), a card offers to save it as a My context piece. It shows under the timer while your prompt is written, and moves under the result if the prompt finishes first. It works in Quick mode too. Spotting it costs nothing extra: it rides the Read step that already runs.

The interview asks one question at a time, with no limit. A Covered so far checklist ticks off What this is, Key facts, Goals, What changes often, and Leave out. It stops when nothing important is missing, and Save what we have is always on screen.

The finished piece is a clean labeled note built only from what you said. If the cleanup adds a number you never said, your own words are used instead. It saves like any My context piece (so it follows Save on this phone) and gets picked for your next prompt.
You can also start it yourself: 🧱 Save as context in the ⋯ menu on a finished prompt, or Build one with questions in the My context editor (that one works with no key).
If a piece overlaps one you already have, you see old vs new with Update, Keep both, or Skip. Bring in uses the same screen now, so it never overwrites a piece without asking.

⚡ Quick version (faster, lighter) is now one steady chip under the timer for the whole build, not just the first few seconds. Tap it while the prompt is being written and the quick model takes over right away. At 2:00 the countdown shows on that same chip instead of a second button.

Run stats (only when Show run stats is on) now count how far the Save as context offer got: shown, tapped, saved, or not now. A label only, never your words, so reviews can tell if the offer earns its spot.

releases.title: Steady box, words that survive a reload, a clear Stop for Talk it out, fresh limits for a new key, My context on all your devices
items: The words box no longer jerks or snaps around while you type or scroll your results, and you can always see what you're writing.

Talk it out: while the mic is on, a red Tap to stop button with a timer sits at the bottom of the screen, so stopping is always one obvious tap. Stop, fix a word, and tap Talk it out again: new words pick up after your fix. On iPhones with iOS 27, Safari's mic only hears once per page (an Apple bug), so when a second try hears nothing it stops, says why, and hands you to the keyboard mic with one tap instead of pretending to listen. Keep talking makes the ⌨️ Use my keyboard mic button glow so the next tap is clear. A pause no longer glues your last word onto the next one. You can also fix a word by typing while it listens. First time? Start here now explains Talk it out (tap, talk, tap Stop) with a Show me where button.

What you type is kept in this tab only, so a reload or Safari reloading the tab brings it back with a Start fresh button. That includes after you Build: forgot to pick your context? Reload and your words are still there (the prompt isn't kept). Deleted when you empty the box, tap Start fresh, close the tab, or after 30 minutes. Never sent anywhere.
A Gemini key from a different Google account gets its own fresh daily count, so it no longer says Flash is used up because of your other key.

My context has 📋 Copy for Notes and 📥 Bring in: copy your pieces as one note, tap 📝 Open Notes and paste it into a new note, iCloud syncs it, and Bring in reads it back on your iPad or Mac. The note is just your pieces in plain words, no block of code at the end, and an edit you make in Notes comes across. Same titles update, nothing is deleted. (Notes' share sheet kept closing on it, so copy and paste is the main way now; Share another way is still there.)
My context is compact: the pieces you used in your last builds go first, only 3 chips show with +N more for the rest, and long titles stay on one line. A piece you picked always shows.

releases.title: Test lab fixes 11/06-07: bigger halo, honest prompts left, Gemma dropped, key pastes itself
items: Write my prompt's halo now zooms in with a small bounce and its glow breathes twice, so the last answer is impossible to miss. Reduce Motion gets a thicker ring and no movement (Test lab #1).
Run stats' header counts only Flash writes as full prompts left (about 60 a day, not 4,560, which had Gemma's allowance added in) (Test lab #2).

Gemma is dropped: on a real free key both Gemma 4 models sat the full 30 seconds without answering, so every grade waited for nothing and then landed on Flash, spending a Flash write. Grading and the fact list are back on Flash-Lite, which has room for 125+ builds a day (Test lab #3, #4, #5).

Grading never uses Flash: a Flash-Lite grades Normal prompts, and the other Flash-Lite grades Quick prompts, so no model grades its own words. A slow Flash-Lite gets the other one alongside after 12 seconds. Only a key with a single Flash-Lite falls back to one Flash for a Quick grade.
The usage list shows every Flash-Lite on the key with its job, and counts requests that never answered (timed out, busy, slower than a backup).
The grade note and Step by step say who graded and any hand-off before it. The grader bench names the grader on every case and how many cases land more than half a point from Claude's key.
A grade still running when the Check ends updates its Step by step row when it lands, instead of saying Still grading forever. If every grader misses, it says so (Test lab #5).

Key catcher (Test lab 11/07): coming back from AI Studio pastes your key and runs Check key by itself where the browser allows it. iPhone Safari always needs a tap plus its own Paste bubble (Apple's rule), so there Paste my key pulses and the note says so. Once the key works with Remember my key off, Remember wears the white halo and scrolls into view until it's ticked.

Full version after a key (Test lab 11/07): if the prompt on screen is the quick version when the key starts working, a card by the key says it rebuilds the full way in 5 seconds (questions first), with Build it now and Not now. Typing in the box or building yourself calls it off.

Key steps in order: Get my free key is the filled, highlighted step until you come back from AI Studio, then Paste my key takes the highlight. On iPhone and iPad, Paste my key says up front to tap Safari's Paste bubble too.
One thing at a time: Remember my key glows first, and the full-version card comes 3 seconds later, or right away once Remember is ticked. With Remember already on, the card comes right away.

releases.title: Model routing: each job on its best model, Gemma joins the crew
items: Jobs now go to the model that fits them best, all set in one routing table: Flash still writes Normal and Rework prompts, Flash-Lite still asks the questions, writes Quick prompts, and runs the stand-in test.

Gemma 4 joins (when your key has it): it grades prompts and lists your facts. It's a different model family from the writer, so it can't go easy on its own work, and it has a much bigger free daily allowance (about 1,500), so those jobs stop eating Flash-Lite's.
The fact list starts on the smaller, quicker Gemma, and a Flash-Lite jumps in if it takes over 6 seconds, so it never holds you up.
Squeezing My context and adding a missing label keep Flash-Lite first, with Gemma as a backup.
If a Gemma model turns a request down, the next model takes it. A key without Gemma works exactly like before.

My context for everyone (#4): out of dev tools and into the main app, under Build. Saving is opt-in: pieces stay in this tab until you turn on Save on this phone (turning it off deletes them from the phone). A phone that already had saved pieces stays opted in. Each piece shows its size against a 3,800 character cap and turns amber with how far over; its chip says over 3,800 too. Typing past the cap never cuts anything off.

releases.title: Quality crew: fact ledger, stand-in AI, shape up front
items: Fact ledger (#44): while Read and Clean run, another Flash-Lite model lists everything the prompt must keep (facts, numbers, dates, limits, hedges, asks). The phone drops any item your words don't back, Flash writes with the rest as a must-keep list, and then the phone ticks each one off in the finished prompt. Anything missing goes to Polish by name.

Stand-in AI test (#45): in Check, a Flash-Lite model pretends to be the AI that will get your prompt and lists what it would still have to ask or guess. Another Flash-Lite model adds lines only for gaps you already answered, and the phone keeps them only if every original line stayed and no new numbers came in. Up to 2 rounds. Gaps you never answered are never guessed; a note under the prompt tells you what your AI may still ask.

Success + format up front (#46): Read now also suggests what a great result looks like and a fitting format and length, so Flash writes them in the first time. They're marked as suggestions, and your own words always win.

The Flash-Lite work is spread out: Read on the 1st Flash-Lite model, Clean on the 2nd, the ledger on a 3rd when your key has one, the stand-in on the 2nd, and fixes on the 1st. The page now uses up to 3 Flash-Lite models. Flash still only writes.

Fixes from flow bench run 1 (the old flow won both complete pairs): Auto-Repair (#34) no longer has an example phrase to copy ("a daily budget that fits the total"), rewrites added lines in plain English instead of pasting raw sentences with "lol" or Spanish, rejects a fix that leaves a sentence hanging ("totaling.", "each person owes."), and never treats sign-offs like "I think that's it" as dropped details. The fact ledger writes clean facts in plain English, 12 at most; Clean drops "lol". The suggested shape can never make a preference stronger or add safety rules. The stand-in only runs on notes of 60+ words, with an 8 second cap. The flow bench retries a busy flow once and has Rerun failed notes.

Flow bench (dev tools, #47): one button runs the 5 hardest notes (moving day, camping trip, surprise party, potluck, meal prep) through the old flow (like live) and the new flow, with the same answers and without your core or My context. Copy for Claude gives the pairs labeled A and B at random, so Claude scores them blind; Copy reveal says which was which, plus times and checks. About 10 Flash writes.

Step by step: a closed box under the time strip lists every step that ran (Read, Clean, Fact ledger, Ask, Write, Polish, Stand-in AI, and Grade with run stats on), with who did it (Flash-Lite, Flash, or You), how long it took, and what happened. Model names show only with run stats on.

Calmer tracker: the steps are grouped into four sections, Prep (Read, Clean, and the fact ledger), Ask, Write, and Finish (Polish and Check, shown only when either runs). The step inside a section shows on the line under the ring. At Ready, a time strip shows one bar split by how long each part took (Prep, Write, Polish, Check) with a small legend.

Fix: the cooking ring only shows the clock and a short status inside it now (Done, about 0:12 left). The longer part, like "Includes 2s check" or "Total, both rounds", moved just under the ring, so it no longer runs into the ring's edge on phones.
Fix for v2.1.19: at Ready, the line under the tracker goes back to saying how the prompt was written (depth, thinking, busy hours plan) instead of showing the last Check step.

Check now runs on every Normal and Rework prompt (the stand-in), with the grade added when run stats are on. The tracker's Clean step is now called Prep, since it covers Clean and the ledger. Quick mode stays fast: no stand-in.

Flow bench rerun (dev tools, folded in to stay at 5 builds): after Rerun failed notes, Copy for Claude has only the notes that were redone, so Claude does not rescore pairs it already scored. Copy reveal still covers all 5 notes and marks the rerun ones.

Flow bench rerun (folded in to stay at 5 builds): Each pair keeps its A and B letters for the whole run, so scores Claude gave before a rerun still match the reveal. Runs saved before this build keep the letters they already had.
Flow bench rerun (folded in to stay at 5 builds): Your last flow bench run reloads with the page, so Copy reveal and Rerun failed notes still work after a reload.

Flow bench rerun (dev tools, folded in to stay at 5 builds): each errored note gets a rerun tick box in the table, all ticked at first. Untick a note to skip it, and Rerun failed notes redoes only the ticked ones, so a rerun can be just T4 and T2.

Fixes from flow bench run 2 (new flow won 3 of 5): a free strictness guard on the phone flags words that make a preference stricter or more medical than you said (safe, safely, cross-contamination, allergy, celiac, medical, strictly). Polish takes them out, and the fact ledger and the suggested shape can no longer carry them in. A word you said yourself is fine.

Test lab fixes (11/05): the stand-in note now explains itself in plain words (Test run: a stand-in AI read your prompt like your AI will), and the old 2.1.19 run stats check is updated, since the new flow (Clean, fact ledger, shape, Polish, stand-in on 60+ word notes) is for everyone and only the grade needs run stats.

Answer the stand-in (#48, SPEC LOCKED 11/05): each question your AI may still ask gets an answer box under the note. Skip costs nothing, and it never re-checks after. Cheaper than rebuilding: 1 small call instead of 4.

releases.title: Build 3: Start here, stuck nudge, leaving mid-build, prompt cooking
items: Start here: when the app opens, the title's waveform entrance plays first, then one white halo panel pulses around the title, waveform and description, then the page scrolls down to Talk it out and the box, which pulse with ✍️ Start here, then the idea strip comes in. It plays on every open until your first tap, type, paste or Talk it out, then never again. Only a yes/no flag is kept, never anything typed.

Stuck? After the box sits still for about 6 seconds with some words in it, one sentence to finish shows under it, aimed at what your thoughts are missing. Tap it to start that line, 🎲 for another. There's no ✕, so a stray tap can't switch them off: they come back after every quiet stretch.

Leaving mid-build: if a step drops while you're in another app, it tries the same model again when you're back instead of spending a backup. Back before it finishes: it says Picked back up. Finished while you were away: the tab title says Prompt ready and coming back says Ready while you were away.

Prompt cooking: a big ring wraps the timer with a kitchen inside. Your pieces fly in as chips and splash into the pot, the spoon stirs, it bubbles and steams, and the chef talk changes every few seconds. Slow? The lid goes on and rattles. A model handing off: the pot shakes, foam spills, the flames flare and it slides to a new burner. Done: the cloche lifts on your plated prompt with sparkles and the ring turns green. Reduce Motion keeps it still.
Build row: while it works, a longer label like Reading your thoughts... wraps inside the Build button, so Quick and Normal keep their full size and the row doesn't jump.

Test lab: 📋 Copy report for Claude. Mark a check ✗ Broken, type what happened, tap it, and every broken check (Do, Expected, What happened) is on your clipboard, ready to paste into the chat. The Ideas jar is still there as the other option.

releases.title: Build 2: context budget, Rework as round 2
items: My context has a budget: the chip shows about how many tokens your picks add and the % of 1,500.

Past 100%, a build with your key squeezes the picks once with Flash-Lite: every fact stays, filler goes. The chip shows before and after. The short version is memory only, so your saved pieces never change.

Rework is now round 2: your prompt goes back in the box with one What was weak line on top. Change anything, then Build. Round 2 uses your original thoughts and answers plus your edits, with no new questions.
Round 2 shows on the timer with the running total for both rounds, and the card shows the score before and after.
Save to Notes after round 2 keeps your original words with the new prompt. Back to round 1 puts everything back. The old one-question rework in the card is gone.

Ideas tab: Edit on any open idea.
Questions read clearer: the question is bold, the helper lines around it are small and gray.
The intro text on the first screen has room to breathe: each sentence on its own line, open spacing.
My context: the editor opens at its top with the cursor in a title, and a new piece goes first.

Dates stay as you said them: the writer keeps maybe and I think, adds no year, weekday, or month, and doesn't make a preference stronger (no strictly you didn't say). If your own weekday and date don't match, the prompt asks the AI to check instead of picking one. The Heads up note now also catches a weekday that doesn't match its date (Saturday the 30th when the 30th is a Friday).
The Quality check is docked below the bar whenever the number check flags something, and the grader bench runs the real Saturday example (B9) first.
Copy gives the prompt only: My context is no longer tacked on as a block. The writer works in just the facts the request needs, and your core stays at the end.

The full suite still runs on every staging push, in the background, and turns the run red if anything fails.
A pull request from staging into main runs the full suite on what goes live (Promote check), and the main deploy runs it again on both versions.
